```plato
//==
// # Transforms
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Affine and projective transform operations
//  - Elementary transforms
//  - Frame and basis operations
//  - Transform identity statics
//  - Motor operations
//  - Point support
//  - Rigid pose operations
//  - Rotation operations and conversions
//  - TRS transform operations

library Transforms
{
    //==
    // # Affine and projective transform operations
    //
    // Application, composition, inversion, and the widening conversions into the
    // affine and projective transforms of `transforms.types.plato` — the common
    // ground where transforms of different kinds are composed.

    //==
    // Affine transforms — the general linear-plus-translation maps; the common
    // ground every 2D/3D transform above converts into, and the right place to
    // compose mixed transform kinds.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_transformation

    // Apply the affine map to a point (includes the translation row).
    Transform(p: Point2D, a: AffineTransform2D): Point2D
        => p.PositionVector.Transform(a.Matrix).ToPoint;
```

```plato
    // Apply the affine map to a point: row-vector product
    // p' = x Row1 + y Row2 + z Row3 + Row4.
    Transform(p: Point3D, a: AffineTransform3D): Point3D {
        var m = a.Matrix;
        var v = m.Row1 * p.X + m.Row2 * p.Y + m.Row3 * p.Z + m.Row4;
        return (v.X, v.Y, v.Z);
    }
```

```plato
    // Apply the linear part to a displacement (the translation row is skipped).
    Transform(v: Vector3D, a: AffineTransform3D): Vector3D {
        var m = a.Matrix;
        var r = m.Row1 * v.X + m.Row2 * v.Y + m.Row3 * v.Z;
        return (r.X, r.Y, r.Z);
    }
```

```plato
    // Apply the homography: lift to homogeneous coordinates, map, and divide
    // by the resulting weight. Precondition: the point is not mapped onto the
    // line at infinity (weight is non-zero).
    Transform(p: Point2D, t: Transform2D): Point2D {
        var m = t.Matrix;
        var v = m.Row1 * p.X + m.Row2 * p.Y + m.Row3;
        return (v.X / v.Z, v.Y / v.Z);
    }
```

```plato
    // Apply the homography: lift to homogeneous coordinates, map, and divide
    // by the resulting weight. Precondition: the point is not mapped onto the
    // plane at infinity (weight is non-zero).
    Transform(p: Point3D, t: Transform3D): Point3D {
        var v = Number4(p.X, p.Y, p.Z, 1.0).Transform(t.Matrix);
        return (v.X / v.W, v.Y / v.W, v.Z / v.W);
    }
```

```plato
    //==
    // # Rigid pose operations
    //
    // Application, composition, inversion, interpolation, and matrix interchange for
    // the rigid poses of `transforms.types.plato`.

    //==
    // Rigid poses — position plus rotation; the natural "where is this object"
    // transform. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigid_transformation

    // Apply the pose: rotate about the origin, then translate to Position.
    Transform(p: Point2D, pose: Pose2D): Point2D
        => pose.Position + p.PositionVector.Transform(pose.Rotation);
```

```plato

    // Rotate a displacement counter-clockwise by the rotation's angle:
    // (x cos - y sin, x sin + y cos).
    Transform(v: Vector2D, r: Rotation2D): Vector2D {
        var c = r.Angle.Cos;
        var s = r.Angle.Sin;
        return (v.X * c - v.Y * s, v.X * s + v.Y * c);
    }
```

```plato

    // Apply the rotor's sandwich product R v ~R: a rotation by the full angle,
    // via the double-angle identities cos a = s^2 - b^2, sin a = 2 s b.
    Transform(v: Vector2D, r: Rotor2D): Vector2D {
        var c = r.Scalar.Square - r.XY.Square;
        var s = 2.0 * r.Scalar * r.XY;
        return (v.X * c - v.Y * s, v.X * s + v.Y * c);
    }
```

```plato
    //==
    // # TRS transform operations
    //
    // Application, matrix interchange, and the lossy widening/narrowing between a
    // rigid pose and the TRS transforms of `transforms.types.plato`.

    //==
    // TRS transforms — scale, then rotate, then translate. Not closed under
    // composition (rotating a non-uniform scale leaves the TRS family), so
    // compose them through their matrix or affine forms.

    // Apply the transform: scale, rotate, then translate.
    Transform(p: Point2D, t: TrsTransform2D): Point2D
        => ((p.PositionVector * t.Scale).Transform(t.Rotation) + t.Translation).ToPoint;
```
